newsitem.title: UK: Next phase of UK gas competition seen likely Nov 1.
newsitem.headline: Next phase of UK gas competition seen likely Nov 1.

text.p: The next phase of domestic gas competition in the UK may be introduced on November 1 after a meeting of the Domestic Competition Focus Group on Monday morning, industry sources said.

The focus group, which consists of all suppliers licensed to supply gas to domestic consumers as well as BG Plc's Transco and Centrica Plc's BGT and Ofgas itself, expects to make a decision shortly on the date, a spokesman for gas industry regulator Ofgas said.
"Ofgas hopes to publish a consultation document by the end of this month," he said.

A minimum of four months is required between the announcement of the start-up date of the next phase and the date itself. Ofgas has been working hard to get the announcement out by the end of June which suggests a start for the next phase of competition by the beginning of November, industry sources said.
But Ofgas would not confirm such speculation.
The Ofgas spokesman added that he believed the focus group will be discussing start-up dates for all regions.

But it is not yet certain whether the announcement will give dates for all regions, or just for Scotland and the North East of England, expected to be the first areas in the next phase to be opened for competition.

Devon, Cornwall and Somerset were opened for competition in April 1996, with a second pilot area covering Avon, Dorset, Kent and East and West Sussex following in two stages in February and March this year.
